s1.syndrome_frame: Pruritic rash with erythematous annular plaques and perivascular inflammation
salient_findings: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on arms and legs
Superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 70s
Patient has recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma
Patient is receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab
Rash started as an erythematous papule on right arm 2 months after initiation of new immunotherapy regimen
Rash gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs
Patient denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash
Oral terbinafine trial yielded no improvement
Biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils
PAS stain was negative for fungal organisms

raw.rationale: The rash started 2 months after initiation of pembrolizumab and ipilimumab, suggesting a temporal relationship between the immunotherapy regimen and the skin reaction, which is consistent with a drug rash.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic dermatitis
rejected.why: While the biopsy showed numerous eosinophils, the clinical context and temporal relationship with the start of immunotherapy point more strongly towards a drug rash as the primary cause.
